This semi-nomadic Turkic people controlled the steppes of southeastern Europe and Crimea in the 9th and 10th centuries, waging war against the early Rus' state for over two hundred years — who were they?
Pechenegs: Extinct Turkic people. The Pechenegs or Patzinaks, were a semi-nomadic Turkic people from Central Asia who spoke the Pecheneg language.
Serving as the 64th Bishop of Rome from 590 until 604, this former Roman prefect sent missionaries to England, including Augustine of Canterbury — who was he?
Pope Gregory I: 64th Bishop of Rome; head of the Roman Catholic Church from AD 590 to 604.
In October 2021, this U.S. assistant secretary for health became the nation's first openly transgender four-star officer across all eight uniformed services — who is she?
Rachel Levine: American public health official (born 1957)
Also called Nagorno-Karabakh, this breakaway state in the South Caucasus governed land internationally recognized as Azerbaijan's until a 2023 offensive emptied it of its people — what was it?
Republic of Artsakh: Breakaway state in the South Caucasus (1991–2023). The conflict erupted into a full-out war in 1992.
A Yale graduate and Harvard Law alum, this former Navy lawyer to SEAL Team One became Florida's 46th governor and briefly ran for the 2024 Republican nomination — who is he?
Ron DeSantis: Governor of Florida since 2019.
In Buddhism it caps the Noble Eightfold Path, and in the Yoga Sutras of Patanjali it's the eighth and final limb of Ashtanga Yoga — what meditative state is this?
Samadhi: State of meditative consciousness. Samādhi (Pali and Sanskrit: समाधि), in the Indian religions, is a state of meditative consciousness.
Co-leading a pro-Kurdish party to double-digit vote shares in Turkey's 2015 elections, this politician ran for president from behind bars in 2018 after his 2016 imprisonment — who is he?
Selahattin Demirtaş: Turkish politician. Selahattin Demirtaş (born 10 April 1973) is a Kurdish politician, lawyer and author.
Imprisoned and tortured as a young dissident under the Ottomans and once sentenced to death by the French, he went on to become the first president of independent Syria in 1943 — who was he?
This is the act of occupying an empty building or plot you don't own, rent, or have permission to use — often the seed of shanty towns in developing cities — what's it called?
Appointed by Emmanuel Macron in September 2025 after the previous government fell to a no-confidence vote, this politician had previously served as France's minister of the armed forces — who is he?
Sébastien Lecornu: Prime Minister of France since 2025.
Serving as UK Home Secretary before becoming the country's second female Prime Minister in 2016, this Conservative politician represented Maidenhead in Parliament for over two decades — who is she?
Theresa May: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from 2016 to 2019.

Walled off to the east and south by the Carpathians and to the west by the Apuseni Mountains, this historical region sits in central Romania and goes by Erdély in Hungarian and Siebenbürgen in German. What is it?
Transylvania: Historical region in Central Europe. Broader definitions of Transylvania also include the western and northwestern Romanian regions of Crișana and Maramureș, and occasionally Banat.
This Roman goddess of love and beauty was claimed as an ancestor by Julius Caesar through her son Aeneas, survivor of the fall of Troy?
Venus (mythology): Ancient Roman goddess of love, sex and fertility.
This Chinese diplomat served as ambassador to Japan before becoming Minister of Foreign Affairs and later director of the Communist Party's Central Foreign Affairs Commission Office — who is he?
Raised in Liverpool as the half-nephew of a Nazi dictator, this man later fought against his own uncle's regime in the US Navy — who is he, after changing his name postwar?
William Stuart-Houston: Half-nephew of Adolf Hitler (1911–1987)
A Hindu monk who became Uttar Pradesh's longest-serving and first two-term chief minister, he won five straight terms from Gorakhpur after entering parliament at just 26 — who is he?
Yogi Adityanath: Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh since 2017.
Who wrote Universal Declaration of Human Rights?

Universal Declaration of Human Rights → United Nations General Assembly. All 193 member states of the UN have ratified at least one of the nine binding treaties influenced by the Declaration, with the vast majority ratifying four or more.
Which of these four was born earliest?
Eratosthenes (born 276 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
Mikhail Lomonosov (born 1711) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four has been around longest?

Lisp (programming language) (founded 1958) is the earliest of the four. Originally specified in the late 1950s, it is the second-oldest high-level programming language still in common use, after Fortran.
Which of these was founded earliest?
MUMPS (founded 1966) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is a physicist?
Donna Strickland is a physicist. Donna Theo Strickland (born May 27, 1959) is a Canadian optical physicist and pioneer in the field of pulsed lasers.
Who among these is a chemist?
Stephanie Kwolek is a chemist. Stephanie Louise Kwolek (July 31, 1923 – June 18, 2014) was a Polish-American chemist known for inventing Kevlar (poly-paraphenylene terephthalamide).
What is the atomic number of Moscovium?
Moscovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Mc and atomic number 115.
What is the atomic number of Bismuth?
Bismuth is a chemical element; it has symbol Bi and atomic number 83.
In what year was Harold Shipman born?
Harold Shipman: Harold Frederick Shipman (14 January 1946 – 13 January 2004) was an English doctor in general practice and serial killer.
In what year was Fritz Haber born?
Fritz Haber: For this work, Haber has been called one of the most important scientists and industrial chemists in human history.
In what year was Ludwig Wittgenstein born?
Ludwig Wittgenstein: Wittgenstein was born in Vienna into one of Europe's richest families.
In what year did Lewis Carroll die?
Lewis Carroll: An avid puzzler, Carroll created the word ladder puzzle, which he called "Doublets", which was published in Vanity Fair magazine between 1879 and 1881.
In what year did Max Weber die?
Max Weber: Born in Erfurt in 1864, Weber studied law and history in Berlin, Göttingen, and Heidelberg.
In what year was Potassium discovered?
Potassium is a chemical element; it has symbol K (from Neo-Latin kalium) and atomic number 19.
SEPECAT Jaguar: Breguet Aviation. As of 2026, the Jaguar remains in service with only the Indian Air Force.
Which country is Sukhoi Su-17 from?
Sukhoi Su-17: Soviet Union. The Sukhoi Su-17 (Russian: Су-17; NATO reporting name: Fitter) is a variable-sweep wing fighter-bomber developed for the Soviet military.
Who is credited with discovering Pavo?
Pavo (constellation): Petrus Plancius. Pavo is a constellation in the southern sky whose name is Latin for 'peacock'.
Who is credited with discovering Nitroglycerin?
Nitroglycerin: Ascanio Sobrero. It is combined with nitrocellulose to form double-based smokeless powder, used as a propellant in artillery and firearms since the 1880s.
Who is credited with discovering Lithium?
Lithium: Johan August Arfwedson. Lithium (from Ancient Greek: λίθος, líthos, 'stone') is a chemical element; it has symbol Li and atomic number 3.

The only living member of its entire taxonomic order, this nocturnal African mammal digs into termite and ant hills using sharp claws and powerful legs — related distantly to elephants and manatees, what is it?
Aardvark (Orycteropus afer) is a medium-sized, burrowing, nocturnal mammal native to Africa.
Sometimes called emotional blindness, this neuropsychological condition involves trouble identifying or describing one's own feelings, and appears in about half of autistic people. What is it?
Alexithymia (-), also called emotional blindness, is a neuropsychological phenomenon characterized by difficulties processing or describing one's emotions.
Dating back to the Neolithic Revolution around 13,000 BC, this branch of agriculture covers the breeding, feeding, and day-to-day care of livestock raised for meat, milk, or fiber — what's it called?
Animal husbandry is the branch of agriculture concerned with animals that are raised for meat, fibre, milk, or other products.
This American physicist won a share of the 1927 Nobel Prize for an effect, now bearing his name, that demonstrated light's particle nature — who was he?
Arthur Compton (September 10, 1892 - March 15, 1962) was an American physicist who shared the 1927 Nobel Prize in Physics with C. T. R. Wilson.
Grown for its edible taproot in red or golden varieties and closely related to Swiss chard, this vegetable's leaves are eaten too, sold simply as "greens" — which root vegetable?
Beetroot is the taproot portion of a Beta vulgaris subsp.
Ranging from southern Canada down to Oaxaca, Mexico, this North American wild cat sports black bars on its forelegs and a short, bobbed tail. What animal is it?
Bobcat (Lynx rufus), also known as the wildcat, bay lynx, or red lynx, is one of the four extant species within the medium-sized wild cat genus Lynx.
Located between the lower back and the perineum, these two rounded regions of human anatomy are built around the gluteus maximus — the largest muscle in the human body — name this body part?
Buttocks (sing.: buttock) are two rounded portions of the exterior anatomy of humans, located on the posterior of the pelvic region.
This root vegetable owes its typical orange color to beta-carotene, though heirloom varieties can be white, purple, or even black — what vegetable is it?
Originating in Northern China, this spitz-type dog breed is known for a dense double coat that forms a distinctive ruff around the neck — name the breed?
Chow Chow is a spitz-type of dog breed originally from Northern China.
Though it resembles a barn swallow, this medium-sized bird is actually more closely related to hummingbirds than to any swallow, its resemblance being pure convergent evolution — what bird is it?

Common swift (Apus apus) is a medium-sized bird, superficially similar to the barn swallow or house martin but somewhat larger, though not stemming from those passerine species, being in the order Apodiformes.
This transdisciplinary field studies circular causal processes like feedback and recursion, where an action's outcome becomes the input for the next — what field is it?
Cybernetics is the transdisciplinary study of circular causal processes such as feedback and recursion, where the outcomes of actions return as inputs for subsequent actions.

This gut ailment flares up when small pouches in the wall of the large intestine become inflamed, often striking with sudden lower-abdominal pain — fever or bloody stool warns of a complication; what is it?
Diverticulitis is a gastrointestinal disease characterized by inflammation of abnormal pouches - diverticula - that can develop in the wall of the large intestine.
This mammal family includes living species from two genera as well as extinct giants like the woolly mammoth, and was first scientifically described in 1821 — what family is it?

Elephantidae is a family of large, herbivorous proboscidean mammals which includes the living elephants (belonging to the genera Elephas and Loxodonta), as well as a number of extinct genera like Mammuthus (mammoths) and Palaeoloxodon.
Known regionally in Shropshire as the 'plum bird,' this small European finch, scientifically Pyrrhula pyrrhula, was the original bird to carry its common English name — which species?
Eurasian bullfinch (Pyrrhula pyrrhula) is a small passerine bird in the finch family, Fringillidae.
Systematically named methanal and carrying the formula CH2O, this pungent gas turns up in particle board, disinfectants, and lab specimen jars — what is it?

Formaldehyde (for-, US also fr-) (systematic name methanal) is a pungent colorless gas mainly used in the production of industrial resins, such as for particle board, coatings, plastics, pulp, paper, synthetic fibers, and textiles.
Nicknamed 'The Lawyer' and celebrated for his eccentric style, this principal shareholder controlled over 4% of Italy's entire GDP through his automaker — who was he?
Gianni Agnelli (12 March 1921 - 24 January 2003), nicknamed L'Avvocato ('The Lawyer'), was an Italian industrialist and principal shareholder of Fiat.
Born Herman Webster Mudgett, this con artist and killer worked his crimes around the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition, earning the nickname "the Beast of Chicago" — who was he?
H. H. Holmes (May 16, 1861 - May 7, 1896), better known as Dr.

Often called the "father of the Indian nuclear programme," this theoretical physicist founded the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research and the research centre later renamed in his honour. Who was he?
Homi J. Bhabha (30 October 1909 - 24 January 1966) was an Indian nuclear theoretical physicist who is widely credited as the "father of the Indian nuclear programme".

Forming at or below zero degrees Celsius, this naturally occurring crystalline solid is technically classified as a mineral and appears on Earth, other planets, and even in interstellar space — what is it?
Ice is water that is frozen into a solid state, typically forming at or below temperatures of 0 C, 32 F, or 273.15 K.
This Brussels chemist ran a famous five-year willow tree experiment and coined the word 'gas' from the Greek for chaos — who was he?
Jan Baptist van Helmont (12 January 1580 - 30 December 1644) was a chemist, physiologist, and physician from Brussels.
Cousin to the wallaby and wallaroo in the family Macropodidae, this Australian marsupial's biggest member is the red one. What is it?
Kangaroo are marsupials from the subfamily Macropodinae (macropods, meaning "large foot").
Caused by a specific type of waterborne bacteria, this form of atypical pneumonia brings cough, fever, muscle pain, and headache within days of exposure — what's it called?
Legionnaires' disease is a form of atypical pneumonia caused by any species of Legionella bacteria, quite often Legionella pneumophila.

Fatigue, memory problems, breathlessness, and sleep trouble that the WHO marks as setting in three months after infection — symptoms that vanish and reappear for weeks or years. What condition is this?
Long COVID is a group of health problems persisting or developing after an initial period of COVID19 from 2 infection.
This Silicon Valley venture capitalist co-created the pioneering Mosaic browser, co-founded Netscape, and later became an advisor to Donald Trump in 2024 — who is he?
Marc Andreessen (an-; born July 9, 1971) is an American businessman, venture capitalist, and former software engineer.
Sold dissolved in solution or shipped anhydrous in pressurized railcars, this simplest primary amine reeks like rotten fish — what compound is it?
Methylamine is an organic compound with a formula of CH5N or CH3NH2.
First documented with ice cream and water by a Tanzanian student and his professor in the 1960s, this contested observation says warmer liquids can outrace colder ones to freezing — what's it called?
Mpemba effect is the observation that very hot liquids or colloids (such as ice cream) can freeze more quickly than colder ones, for similar volumes and surrounding conditions.
Found in tobacco and trace amounts of tomatoes and eggplants, this nightshade alkaloid is used recreationally as a stimulant yet acts as a deadly neurotoxin to insects — what is it?
Nicotine is an alkaloid found primarily in plants of the nightshade family, notably in tobacco; it is also synthesized.
These red-haired great apes once roamed all of Southeast Asia but now cling to just Borneo and Sumatra — and in 2017 scientists confirmed a brand-new third species among them. Which animal is it?
Orangutan are great apes native to the rainforests of Indonesia and Malaysia.
This British theoretical physicist, one of the founders of quantum mechanics, coined the term 'quantum electrodynamics' and shared the 1933 Nobel Prize in Physics with Erwin Schrödinger — who is he?
Paul Dirac (dih-RAK; 8 August 1902 - 20 October 1984) was a British theoretical physicist who is considered to be one of the founders of quantum mechanics.
This branch of linguistics is concerned with how speech sounds are physically produced, transmitted as sound waves, and perceived by listeners — name the field?
Phonetics is a branch of linguistics that mainly concerns the articulation, sound wave properties, and perception of speech sounds.
Native to Southeast Asia and a natural, non-hybrid ancestor of both the grapefruit and the bitter orange, this largest of all citrus fruits also goes by the name 'shaddock' — what is it?
Pomelo (PUM-; or pummelo, Citrus maxima), also known as a shaddock, is the largest citrus fruit.
Which industry has expanded from traditional books and newspapers to e-books, websites, and video games, with giants like Thomson Reuters and News Corp among its biggest players?
Publishing is the process of making information, literature, music, software, and other content, whether in physical or digital form, available to the public for sale or free of charge.
This long-term autoimmune disorder leaves joints warm, swollen and painful — typically the same ones on both sides of the body — and can stiffen worse after rest. What is it?
Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a long-term autoimmune disorder that primarily affects joints.
Which genus of 20 to 30 species of flowering plants in the family Adoxaceae produces both a fragrant white flower cluster and a dark berry, each with their own distinct common name?

Sambucus is a genus of between 20 and 30 species of flowering plants in the family Adoxaceae. The various species are commonly referred to as elder, with the flowers as elderflower, and the fruit as elderberry.
Cartilaginous and toothy, these fish are the sister group to the rays and skates and trace their ancestors to the Devonian Period — what are they?

Shark are a group of elasmobranch cartilaginous fishes characterized by a ribless endoskeleton, dermal denticles, five to seven gill slits on each side, and pectoral fins that are not fused to the head.
These eight-legged arachnids inject venom through their fangs and extrude silk from spinnerets, ranking as the largest order in their class — what are they?
Spider (order Araneae) are air-breathing arthropods that have eight limbs, chelicerae with fangs generally able to inject venom, and spinnerets that extrude silk.

Practiced by professionals who determine property boundaries and construction points using total stations, GNSS receivers, and lidar sensors, which technical discipline combines geometry, trigonometry, and law?
Surveying is the technique, profession, art, and science of determining the terrestrial positions of points based on the distances and angles between them.

Proposed by Albert Einstein in special and general forms published in 1905 and 1915, this framework superseded 200-year-old Newtonian mechanics and explains gravitation's relation to the other forces of nature — name it?
Theory of relativity comprises two physics theories by Albert Einstein: special relativity and general relativity. Special relativity applies to all physical phenomena in the absence of gravity.
Formed from glycerol bonded to three fatty acids, these molecules make up the main constituents of body fat in humans and are also major components of human skin oil — what are they?
Triglyceride (from tri- and glyceride; also TG, triacylglycerol, TAG, or triacylglyceride) is an ester derived from glycerol and three fatty acids.
Known also as sight or eyesight, this sense lets the body detect photons and build a picture of its environment using daytime or night modes — what is it?
Visual perception is the ability to detect light and use it to form an image of the surrounding environment.
Known for a rapid side-to-side flight just before landing and living only in colonies, these black-and-yellow social wasps of the genera Vespula and Dolichovespula go by what North American name?
Yellowjacket is the common name in North America for predatory social wasps of the genera Vespula and Dolichovespula.
A rapid rise-and-fall of voltage across a cell membrane, this "spike" depolarizes neighboring spots and is how neurons and muscle cells fire — what is this electrical event called?
Action potential: Neuron communication by electric impulses.
Beginning about six hours after someone dependent on drinking stops, this set of symptoms can include shaking, sweating, seizures, and life-threatening delirium -- what is it called?
Formed when hydrogen atoms in ammonia are swapped out for carbon-based groups, which class of nitrogen-containing organic compounds includes aniline as its simplest aromatic member?
Amine: Chemical compounds and groups containing nitrogen with a lone pair (:N)
Native to Africa, India, the Middle East and Central Asia, these fleet-footed members of the family Bovidae aren't actually one single evolutionary group — what are they?
Pinned by a boulder in a Utah canyon in 2003, this mountaineer amputated his own forearm with a dull pocket knife to survive, later portrayed by James Franco in a film — who is he?
Delivered to the RAF starting in 1956, this delta-wing strategic bomber was considered the most advanced but riskiest of Britain's three V bombers — which aircraft?
Avro Vulcan: British jet-powered delta wing strategic bomber.
Nicknamed 'top shelf' dizziness, this inner-ear disorder causes brief spinning sensations lasting under a minute whenever you tilt or turn your head — what is this condition called?
Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo: Medical condition. Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV), sometimes called "top shelf vertigo", is a disorder arising from a problem in the inner ear.
This medical term for blood escaping the circulatory system describes a healthy person as able to lose 10 to 15 percent of their total volume without serious harm — what is it called?
Bleeding: Blood escaping from the circulatory system. Bleeding, hemorrhage, haemorrhage or blood loss, is blood escaping from the circulatory system from damaged blood vessels.
Making up just 2.6 percent of the brain's weight, this stalk-like structure connects the cerebrum to the spinal cord and houses all ten pairs of cranial nerve origins — what is it?
Brainstem: Posterior part of the brain, adjoining and structurally continuous.
Its Latin name means "chisel-bearing," a nod to the stout egg-laying organs of its members — which insect suborder includes grasshoppers, ground-hoppers, and pygmy mole crickets?
Caelifera: Suborder of insects. The latter should not be confused with the mole crickets (Gryllotalpidae), which belong to the other Orthopteran suborder Ensifera.
A founder of humanistic psychology, this American psychologist pioneered person-centered therapy, an approach that also shaped student-centered learning in education — who is he?
Certified in 1984 and developed into a freighter variant for FedEx, this single-engine turboprop utility plane typically seats nine and can be fitted with floats or skis — which aircraft?
Cessna 208 Caravan: Family of utility transport aircraft.
Blooming in autumn and closely associated with the month of November, this East Asian flowering genus in the daisy family boasts thousands of horticultural varieties — which flower?
Chrysanthemum: Genus of flowering plants in the daisy family.

Triggered by an abnormal immune response to gluten found in wheat, barley, and rye, this chronic autoimmune condition mainly affects the small intestine and often causes malabsorption in children — which condition?
Coeliac disease: Autoimmune disorder. Coeliac disease (Commonwealth English) or celiac disease (American English) is a chronic autoimmune disease, mainly affecting the small intestine.
Also known as the Cornelian cherry, this dogwood-family shrub or small tree is native to western and southern Europe as well as southwestern Asia — what's its scientific name?
Cornus mas: Species of flowering plant in the family Cornaceae.
Also called Bermuda grass, this hardy warm-climate turf species is ironically not native to the island of the same name — which plant, by its scientific name?
Cynodon dactylon: Species of grass. Cynodon dactylon, commonly known as Bermuda grass or as couch grass in Australia and New Zealand, is a grass found worldwide in warm and tropical climates.
This central nervous system stimulant is the 'right-handed' mirror-image form of a well-known molecule, prescribed for ADHD and narcolepsy and sometimes given as an inactive prodrug — what is it?
Dextroamphetamine: CNS stimulant and isomer of amphetamine.
A broad-spectrum member of the tetracycline class, this antibiotic treats everything from acne and chlamydia to Lyme disease and cholera — though it'll make you sunburn more easily. Which drug?
Doxycycline: Tetracycline-class antibiotic. It is used to treat bacterial pneumonia, acne, chlamydia infections, Lyme disease, cholera, typhus, and syphilis, and is sometimes used to prevent malaria.
This unit of energy equals the kinetic energy a single electron gains while crossing an electric potential difference of one volt — what is it called?
Sometimes abbreviated ETM, this antibiotic treats everything from respiratory infections to syphilis and is the eye ointment routinely dabbed on newborns to prevent eye infections. What is it?
Erythromycin: Antibiotic medication. Erythromycin (sometimes abbreviated ETM in reports) is an antibiotic used for the treatment of a number of bacterial infections.
Native to the Iberian Peninsula and introduced to hundreds of locations worldwide, this grassland herbivore digs extensive burrow networks called warrens — what is it?
Found on the forelimbs of most tetrapods, these prehensile, often opposable digits give primates like humans their dexterity for grasping and fine movement — what are they called?

This German chemist won a Nobel Prize for inventing a process that synthesizes ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen gas — a breakthrough that today supports nearly half the world's food production. Who is he?

A Belgian Catholic priest and physicist, he was first to argue that the recession of galaxies proves an expanding universe, and proposed a 'primeval atom' — the first version of the Big Bang theory. Who was he?
Georges Lemaître: Belgian scientist and Catholic priest (1894–1966)
This term describes the overall system of rules, processes, and power structures that steers decision-making within an organized group — what is it?
Governance: Processes of interacting with people and making decisions.
Occurring in any of the senses, this perception feels completely real despite the absence of any actual external stimulus — what is it?
Hallucination: Perception that only seems real.
With over 800 species lugging borrowed snail shells to shield their soft, non-calcified abdomens, this crustacean is essentially homeless without a hand-me-down home. What is it?
Stretching about a meter from crown to tail-tip, this deep-blue South American parrot is the largest of its kind and can be mistaken for a smaller relative — which vulnerable parrot?
Co-creator of the AlexNet neural network and former chief scientist at OpenAI, this computer scientist has won NeurIPS's Test of Time Award three years running — who is he?

This Mexican neurophysiologist studied shamanism, meditation, and telepathy through the scientific method, wrote more than 50 books on the subjects, and then vanished without a trace in December 1994 — who was he?
Jacobo Grinberg: Mexican pseudoscientist, neurophysiologist and psychologist.
This English mathematician dreamed up the cellular automaton known as the Game of Life and spent his later years at Princeton — who was he?
Also called Bushman's tea, the leaves of this East African shrub are chewed as a recreational stimulant, most popular among Somalis and Yemenis — what is it?

This trigonometric relationship links each side of a triangle to the angle across from it, with every such ratio equal to twice the radius of the triangle's circumscribed circle. What is the rule called?
Law of sines: Property of all triangles on a Euclidean plane.
Patented in 1978 and approved for use in the US in 1987, this ACE inhibitor is a common first-line treatment for high blood pressure — what drug is it?
Lisinopril: Medication used to treat hypertension and heart failure.
This American biologist argued that cells with nuclei arose from symbiotic mergers of bacteria, and co-developed the Gaia hypothesis with James Lovelock — who was she?

Raising silkworms at 13 and publishing a two-volume study of caterpillars, this German-Dutch artist was among the earliest European naturalists to document insects from direct observation — who was she?
Maria Sibylla Merian: German naturalist and artist (1647–1717)
Comprising 18 to 24 species that hybridize freely where their ranges overlap, this genus of the mint family thrives in wet, moist soils worldwide — what is it?
Mentha: Genus of flowering plants in the family Lamiaceae.
Based on a Soviet fighter jet but optimized for ground attack, this variable-sweep aircraft was license-built in India as the 'Bahadur,' or 'Valiant' — which jet?
Mikoyan MiG-27: Series of 1970s Soviet attack aircraft.
Grown to feed silkworms for commercial silk production, this fast-growing tree releases its pollen at more than half the speed of sound — which species?
Morus alba: Plant species in the fig family.
Divided in two by a central septum, this air-filled space sits behind the nose and forms the uppermost part of the respiratory system — what is it?
Nasal cavity: Large, air-filled space above and behind the nose in the middle of the face.
A child prodigy turned MIT mathematician, this American is regarded as the originator of cybernetics — the science of communication in living things and machines — who was he?
Norbert Wiener: American mathematician and philosopher (1894–1964)

Found above 3,500 metres on the Tibetan Plateau, this parasitic fungus grows out of moth larvae and is prized — despite containing arsenic — as an aphrodisiac in traditional Chinese medicine. What is it commonly called?
Ophiocordyceps sinensis: Species of fungus. It parasitizes larvae of ghost moths and produces a fruiting body which is valued in traditional Chinese medicine and Nepalese medicine as an aphrodisiac.
From a single western-Mediterranean flowering plant come both a notorious drug and the tiny dark seeds sprinkled on your bagel — which species is it?
Papaver somniferum: Species of flowering plant in the poppy family.
A hybrid cross of watermint and spearmint, this herb is one of the oldest used in cooking and medicine and a key plant source of menthol — what is it?
Peppermint: Hybrid flowering plant in the family Lamiaceae.
Enclosed in a papery husk derived from its calyx, this nightshade genus includes the tomatillo and Cape gooseberry among its edible-fruited species — which genus?

The most common hormonal disorder in women of reproductive age, it's diagnosed by two of three signs — irregular periods, high testosterone, or many antral follicles — despite a name that misleadingly implies true cysts. What's its newer name?
Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome: Hormonal disorder in women. The exact cause of PMOS remains uncertain.
Native to Eurasia and known by the common names 'cherry plum' and 'myrobalan plum,' this species is thought to be a parent of the cultivated plum — what is it, scientifically?
Prunus cerasifera: Species of plum. Native to Eurasia and naturalized elsewhere, P. cerasifera is believed to be one of the parents of the cultivated plum.
Built from bases including uracil, adenine, guanine, and cytosine, this molecule can serve as a template for building proteins or catalyze reactions itself — what is it?
RNA: Family of large biological molecules.
This branch of medicine handles more than 100 inflammatory diseases of the bones, muscles, and joints — like lupus and arthritis — and overlaps heavily with immunology. What is it?
Rheumatology: Medical speciality of inflammatory diseases.
Known as 'swede' in British English, this root vegetable is a hybrid of cabbage and turnip — what is it?
Rutabaga: Root vegetable in the Brassica family.
Usually forming an S- or C-shaped curve with a rotational twist, this sideways irregular curvature of the spine sits alongside kyphosis and lordosis among the spine's abnormal curves. What is it?
Scoliosis: Left-right asymmetry of the spine's curvature.
This Japanese army medical officer led a biological and chemical warfare unit in Japanese-occupied Manchuria during World War II and was later granted immunity — who is he?
Shirō Ishii: Japanese biological weapons specialist (1892–1959)
Famous for a repetitive, melodic call often referenced in poetry, this brown, spotted-breasted bird uses a favorite stone as an 'anvil' to crack open snail shells — which species?
Song thrush: Species of bird. The song thrush (Turdus philomelos) is a thrush that breeds across the West Palearctic.
Fired by Apple's board in 1985, he founded NeXT and bought a animation studio before returning a decade later to revolutionize consumer tech. Who?
Steve Jobs: American businessman and inventor (1955–2011)
Serving as prime minister of Turkey seven separate times before becoming president from 1993 to 2000, he was also the first PM to have been born in the Turkish Republic — who was he?
